Plus Wile E Coyote returns to the big screen Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here Martin Belam Fri 14 Aug 2026 07.35 EDT Last modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 07.51 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. The extent to which federal law enforcement targeted political opponents and peaceful organizers has been laid bare in newly disclosed court documents . Internal investigative files reveal that the Department of Homeland Security launched a sweeping surveillance operation against anti-ICE protesters, major labor unions and left-leaning advocacy groups – sending undercover agents to infiltrate community meetings and issuing administrative subpoenas to seize financial records. The documents show that DHS investigators obtained financial records of unions and non-profits, as part of an inquiry into “domestic terrorist financing”. What did undercover government agents do? They infiltrated community meetings, joined private activist Signal chats and surreptitiously recorded audio at local events – including a “resistance skills training” at a public library and a sparring session at a church gym, where an agent accidentally dropped his recording device. Agents posed as activists and actively engaged participants by offering to help with “direct-action” protests. How have activists responded? Emilia González Avalos, the executive director of Unidos MN, a Minneapolis social justice non-profit group, said: “I believe that this is a clear attempt to intimidate us, to punish and politically repress disagreement and difference. And that is not the America that we have built through hundreds of years. And it’s definitely not the America that we are organizing for.” Crimea bomb kills ‘Ukrainian sub commander who defected’ View image in fullscreen A portrait of Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin, in Sevastopol, where the attack took place. Photograph: Igor Ivanko/AFP/Getty Images A Russian military officer labelled as a Ukrainian defector ⁠was killed in a ⁠bomb ​attack on Thursday in Russian-annexed Crimea. Robert Shageyev was described on Russian Telegram channels as ‌a former Ukrainian naval officer who switched allegiance to ‌Russia during Moscow’s annexation of Crimea in 2014 when he was commanding Ukraine’s only submarine, the Zaporizhzhia. Where did the attack take place? The attack took place in Sevastopol, the biggest city in Russian-annexed Crimea. ​The regional governor, Mikhail Razvozhayev, said a woman had been arrested on suspicion of ⁠assassinating Shageyev on behalf of Ukrainian special services. What has Poland said about Russian activity there? A Russian plan to kill a Ukrainian American citizen in Warsaw was thwarted by Poland before it could be carried out, the Polish prime minister has said . Donald Tusk said it was the first time that “someone on the order of Russia” had sought to attack a US citizen on the territory of another Nato country. Massachusetts teen accused of killing mother and brother used ChatGPT View image in fullscreen Arjun Aravind listens as his lawyer Debra DeWitt speaks. Photograph: Lane Turner/The Boston Globe/AP A Massachusetts teenager accused of killing his mother and younger brother is being held without bail as authorities investigate a double-murder case that prosecutors say is connected to his use of ChatGPT . Arjun Aravind, 17, appeared for his arraignment in Concord district court on Thursday morning, where a not-guilty plea to murder and several additional charges was entered on his behalf. What did the county district attorney say? Marian Ryan said in a press conference: “The investigation has so far shown that Arjun had recently been demonstrating some concerning behavior, including using the internet and ChatGPT to make searches for theoretical ideas or fantasy stories regarding the killing of his family.” WNBA condemns ‘bad-faith’ efforts to fuel transgender player debate View image in fullscreen Golden State Valkyries’ Tiffany Hayes, front, steals the ball from Chicago Sky’s Gabriela Jacquez in the first half of a WNBA basketball game in San Francisco. Photograph: Carlos Avila Gonzalez/San Francisco Chronicle/AP The WNBA on has criticized those trying to create a narrative about transgender women playing in the league . A league spokesperson said “There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others.” The statement came hours after an anti-hate taskforce met virtually and discussed a variety of topics, including social media vitriol and transgender athletes. There has never been a trans woman – a person assigned male at birth who transitions to align with their gender identity – on a WNBA roster. In other news … View image in fullscreen Count Binface gestures while standing with other candidates after Reform UK party leader Nigel Farage was declared the winner. Photograph: Jack Taylor/Reuters Trump-aligned British politician Nigel Farage has won a special election in England and will return to parliament, having defeated 33 fringe and novelty candidates. He failed to turn up to hear the result. A man with a bin on his head pretending to be from outer space came second. Trump orders Pentagon to redesign US aircraft carrier to use steam catapults to launch jets saying digital systems are too ‘complicated’. Max Miller’s ex-wife is suing him for uploading a picture of their infant daughter to a publicly accessible Dropbox folder as part of their custody battle. A Guatemalan immigrant detained by ICE at a Newark, New Jersey has died , the third person to die after being held at Delaney Hall. The board of the John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington is said to have voted once again to inscribe Donald Trump’s name on the facade of its building . Stat of the day: Severe storms cut power supply to 540,000 homes in US midwest View image in fullscreen Crews work among trees and power lines downed by severe storms. Photograph: Carolyn Kaster/AP Power supply was cut on Thursday ⁠to about 540,000 homes and businesses across the US midwest as severe storms battered the region. Indiana ⁠was the ​hardest-hit state, with more than 267,000 outages, representing about 8% of its roughly 3.3 million customers. Photograph: Jiji Press/EPA At least four people died in eastern Japan after “unprecedented” heavy rain left nearly 7,000 stranded at Tokyo’s Narita airport, and forced thousands to take refuge in government buildings. The torrential rains hit Chiba prefecture, east of Tokyo, triggering landslide warnings and power outages. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: Hours after the shootout, Volodymyr Zelenskyy (above) fired the SBU’s head of the department for the protection of state secrets. Photograph: DTS News Agency Germany/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Hours after the shootout, Volodymyr Zelenskyy (above) fired the SBU’s head of the department for the protection of state secrets. Photograph: DTS News Agency Germany/Shutterstock Ukraine Shootout in Kyiv between Ukrainian spy services ‘disgraceful’, says Zelenskyy Domestic security service says clash with military intelligence directorate ‘definitely shouldn’t have happened’ Amy Hawkins in Kyiv Thu 3 Sep 2026 10.04 EDT Last modified on Thu 3 Sep 2026 11.08 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Several people have been injured in a shootout in central Kyiv between two branches of Ukraine’s security services, in an incident Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “disgraceful”. The shootout, which took place on Wednesday morning in a downtown area of the capital, was between officers from the domestic security service, the SBU, and the military intelligence directorate, the HUR. The SBU said in a statement on Thursday that the shootout “definitely shouldn’t have happened” and that it was assisting state investigators. The clash appears to have been sparked by the SBU’s recent arrest of a Russian man fighting for Ukraine under the supervision of the HUR. Local media reported that while the SBU was searching an apartment linked to the investigation, HUR officers arrived and shots were fired; three HUR officers were injured. The SBU said that, together with the HUR, it had foiled a Russian-backed terrorist plot targeting a Russian opposition leader who had recently arrived in Ukraine. In a separate statement, the SBU said its officers had come under armed attack while conducting an investigation and they had used their weapons in response. On Thursday, the SBU released a video of the Russian national fighting for Ukraine who had been arrested last month. In the video, the man says he was contacted by a person from Russia acting for Moscow’s intelligence agency who wanted to recruit him to assassinate Ukrainian defence personnel and other individuals. The man’s lawyer told local media that the video had been recorded under pressure and was being released to “whitewash” the shootout. The man has since been released from SBU custody. Hours after the shootout, Zelenskyy fired the SBU’s head of the department for the protection of state secrets, Oleh Khramov. “Shooting here in Ukraine is permitted only at Russian occupiers, in defence of Ukraine. Our state will never regard any other shootout as acceptable,” Zelenskyy wrote in a social media post. The incident comes at a delicate moment for Zelenskyy. He has recently faced down calls from a sacked defence minister to hold wartime elections . The demand, from Mykhailo Fedorov – whose dismissal triggered a wave of protests – was the biggest challenge to Zelenskyy’s authority from inside Ukraine since the start of the Russian invasion. Zelenskyy also recently sacked a presidential deputy chief of staff amid reports she was being investigated in connection to an alleged money-laundering scheme. The president said the shooting on Wednesday needed to be investigated by both the SBU and the HUR. Ukraine’s main investigative agency has also opened an investigation. In a separate incident, a 71-year-old man was shot outside a medical clinic on Thursday morning in Kyiv and remains in a “serious condition”, according to the the Kyiv city prosecutor’s office. An investigation has been launched into an attempted murder. The shootings come as Kyiv withstands an intense period of Russian bombardment . Air raid alerts have been active for extended periods in the daytime as well as overnight in the capital. Across the country, at least five people were killed in strikes on Wednesday night. Ukraine is facing a critical shortage of US-made ​Patriot interceptors capable ⁠of shooting down Russian ballistic missiles. Ukraine has also increased its use of long-range drones to target deep into Russian territory. This week Zelenskyy said that Russian airspace was becoming unsafe for commercial airlines because of the growing number of drone attacks. On Thursday, Russian media reported that the military officer who ordered a missile strike on the Okhmatdyt children’s hospital in Kyiv in July 2024 had been shot. Maj Gen Nikolai Varpakhovich was reportedly shot twice by an assailant riding a motorbike and wearing a helmet. The officer remains in a critical condition. https://telex.hu/after/2026/09/03/petran.text: Menü Kereső Petrányi Viktóriát nevezték ki a magyar filmreformért felelős miniszteri biztossá After Dévai László Tarr Zoltán társadalmi kapcsolatokért és kultúráért felelős miniszter Petrányi Viktória filmproducert nevezte ki filmreformért felelős miniszteri biztossá – jelentette be a miniszter a Facebookon. Tarr szerint a magyar filmpiacot az előző vezetés elhanyagolta és bizonytalanságba sodorta, miközben Magyarországnak kulturális és gazdasági szempontból is fontos szerepe van a nemzetközi filmiparban. Petrányi Viktória több mint két évtizedes tapasztalattal rendelkezik a magyar és a nemzetközi filmgyártásban, és társalapítója Magyarország egyik legnagyobb filmgyártó cégének, a Proton Cinemának. Tarr azt írta, a producer saját szakmai karrierjét háttérbe helyezve vállalta el a miniszteri biztosi feladatot. Petrányi egyik legfontosabb feladata a magyar filmtámogatási rendszer megújításához szükséges intézkedések összehangolása lesz. Emellett felügyeli a jelenlegi rendszer működésének és döntéshozatali folyamatainak átvilágítását, valamint részt vesz a filmipar átalakításával kapcsolatos társadalmi és szakmai egyeztetésekben. A miniszteri biztos feladata lesz az iparági fejlesztések és reformok előkészítése, valamint szakmai felügyelete is. Tarr szerint sok feladat áll még a kormány előtt a magyar film megújításában, ezért örül annak, hogy ezt a munkát Petrányi Viktóriára bízhatja. Kövess minket Facebookon is! Követem! Friss az Afteren

https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Wife of Australian detained by Vietnam says she has concerns about his welfare Chloe Dang, the wife of a missing Vietnamese Australian democracy campaigner, said she hasn’t slept for days after her husband went missing during a trip to Cambodia. Tran Hiep, 50, was due to return to Bangkok, Thailand, earlier this month and reunite with his wife, but never returned. Dang said the government has since confirmed he has been detained by Vietnamese authorities on what have been described as “fabricated” charges. Dang said she hasn’t heard anything from her husband, but found out yesterday from Vietnam that he was in the country. She said she does not know where he is being held, or the status of his wellbeing. “My most concern is his wellbeing as well, because it’s been 12 days and we hadn’t heard anything,” she told ABC News Breakfast. “He’s an Australian citizen.
